name: ACON

paper.title: ACON: Optimizing Context Compression for Long-horizon LLM Agents

construction.unit: one structured history summary (REASONING, VARS, TODO, COMPLETED, GUARDRAILS in the optimized AppWorld guideline); optionally a refined version of each long observation
construction.kept_as: LLM-compressed text that replaces the raw history; the last action-observation pair stays raw
construction.processing: compressor LLM follows a natural-language guideline optimized offline from contrasts between full-context and compressed runs
construction.writer: compressor LLM (gpt-4.1, gpt-4.1-mini, or a LoRA-distilled Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-8B or Phi-4)

organization.structure: single summary block in the prompt, followed by the kept and newer turns

management.operations: when history passes the threshold, the compressor rewrites previous summary + older turns into a new summary that replaces the old one and a new session starts
management.forgetting: raw turns are dropped after being summarized; long observations are replaced by their refined version

retrieval.candidates: none: the whole compressed context is in the prompt
retrieval.budget: history compressed above 4,096 tokens (AppWorld, OfficeBench) or 2,048 (QA); observations above 1,024 / 512 / 400 tokens

use.context: system prompt + task + <HISTORY_SUMMARY> + last kept turn and newer turns (+ refined observation in observation mode)
use.reasoning: ReAct agent: one thought and action per step

classify.note: Memory is one rolling summary inside the agent's prompt; each compression rewrites the previous summary together with the older turns. The contribution is how the compression instruction is learned, not how memory is searched.

stages.ingestion: Each agent step adds a thought/action and the tool's observation to the interaction history.
stages.construction: When the history passes a token threshold, a compressor LLM rewrites it into a structured summary; separately, any observation longer than its own threshold is rewritten into a shorter refined observation before it enters the history.
stages.organization: No store outside the prompt: a new session holds the system prompt, the task, the summary and the last raw action-observation pair.
stages.update: Each later compression reads the previous summary plus the turns since then and writes a summary that replaces it.
stages.answer: The ReAct agent reads its whole compressed context at every step.
stages.learning: The compressor's guideline is optimized offline: o3 reads trajectories where full context succeeded but compression failed, writes feedback, and proposes 5 revised guidelines, of which the best on training tasks is kept (UT); an optional second pass trims content that successful compressed runs never used (CO). The compressor can then be distilled into a small model with LoRA.

summary: Compresses a long-horizon agent's history and long tool outputs with an LLM whose instruction is refined offline from failures caused by compression, then distils that compressor into small models.
notes: Venue checked: ICML 2026 main-conference poster (icml.cc/virtual/2026/poster/66270; PDF footer 'Proceedings of the 43rd ICML, PMLR 306'). Paper text from arXiv v3 (1 Jun 2026). Code: official repo microsoft/acon at d63f9ae (2025-10-14), the only commit after the initial one; it predates v3 by eight months. Two variants: history compression and observation compression, each after the UT step or UT+CO steps; they are run separately in the main tables (combined in App. Table 14).

sources.code_note: Official repo named in the paper. d63f9ae (2025-10-14) is the latest of two commits, both from October 2025, so it matches arXiv v1 rather than the ICML version (v3, 2026-06). The repo ships the unoptimized starting guidelines and the optimizer scripts, not the optimized guidelines; those are printed in App. D.

headline: ACON is prompt optimization for a summarizer: the memory itself is one rolling summary that replaces the raw history once it passes 4,096 tokens.
The guideline is learned from contrast pairs: tasks the agent solves with full context but fails after compression.
On AppWorld with gpt-4.1, UTCO history compression keeps accuracy (56.5 vs 56.0) at 26% lower peak tokens (7.33k vs 9.93k).

open_questions: Main tables apply history or observation compression alone; combining them (App. Table 14) drops AppWorld accuracy to 44.6-45.8, so the two do not simply add up.
A second UT round after UT+CO lowers AppWorld accuracy to 47.0 (Table 14), and only one round is run; how stable the optimization is across seeds or reruns is not reported.
FIFO and retrieval baselines keep a fixed number of turns rather than matching ACON's token budget, so part of the gap may be the budget rather than the guideline.

discussion.takeaway: An agent's history can be replaced by an LLM summary without losing accuracy if the summarizer's instruction is tuned on the failures that compression causes; the tuned summarizer can run on a small model.

claims.claim: ACON cuts peak tokens by 26-54% while beating other compression baselines.
claims.evidence: AppWorld history UTCO 56.5 at 7.33k peak vs 56.0 at 9.93k with no compression and 43.5 for naive prompting (Table 1); 8-objective QA peak 10.35k → 4.65k (Table 2b).

claims.claim: Optimized compressors distil into small models with little loss.
claims.evidence: Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-8B and Phi-4 compressors keep over 95% of the gpt-4.1 teacher's accuracy. Fig. 4

claims.claim: Compression helps small agents by removing distraction.
claims.evidence: Distilled Qwen3-14B agent: AppWorld 25.6 → 33.9 (+32%), 8-objective QA EM 0.158 → 0.230 (+46%). Fig. 5, §4.4

claims.claim: Contrastive feedback and a strong optimizer matter.
claims.evidence: o3 with contrast 51.2 vs 50.6 without contrast and 47.6 with gpt-4.1 as optimizer. Table 3

claims.claim: Moderate thresholds give the best trade-off.
claims.evidence: 4,096 for history and 1,024 for observations on AppWorld. Fig. 6

limits: Experiments mostly use GPT models; other model families are untested.
Benchmarks are controlled environments, not live deployments.
Natural-language guideline optimization has no convergence guarantee.
Distilled students still trail the teacher; training data is about 100 examples per domain.
Compression adds latency and invalidates the KV cache of the history.
reading: UT beats UTCO on OfficeBench (74.74 vs 72.63) and QA EM (0.373 vs 0.335) but loses on AppWorld (51.2 vs 56.5); the paper picks the variant per environment after seeing test results, so no single setting wins everywhere.
On AppWorld only UTCO history compression matches no compression (56.5 vs 56.0); UT history (51.2) and both observation variants (47.0, 53.6) stay below it.

The FIFO baseline keeps the last 5 turns and Retrieval keeps 4 retrieved turns plus the last one; these are not set to ACON's token budget, and FIFO scores 84.2 on easy AppWorld tasks, above ACON UT (77.2).
Latency per task rises with compression (73.2 s → 87.7 s history, 101.9 s observation) even though API cost falls (Table 4).
The public code predates the ICML version by eight months and does not include the optimized guidelines used for the tables.

abstract.text: Long-horizon LLM agents accumulate an ever-growing log of actions and observations, which raises memory cost and distracts the model. ACON compresses both the interaction history and long observations with an LLM, and improves the compressor's instructions in natural language: on training tasks, it compares runs that succeed with full context against runs that fail after compression, and an optimizer LLM rewrites the guideline from that feedback. The optimized compressor can then be distilled into smaller models. On AppWorld, OfficeBench and multi-objective QA it lowers peak tokens by 26-54% while doing better than other compression methods, and it helps small models act as agents.
